title: Journey 1: Agentic UI Architectures (A2UI vs. MCP Apps vs. Sandboxed Embeds)
description: Master how declarative A2UI JSONL component streams, MCP Apps (ui:// resources + JSON-RPC postMessage), and Antigravity's native UI controls work under the hood.

nodes.title: 1. Declarative Component Streaming (A2UI) vs. Code-Synthesized Iframes
nodes.objective: Distinguish between streaming declarative JSON component blueprints (A2UI) and serving executable HTML/JS bundles inside sandboxed iframes (MCP Apps & agent-embed).

primaryModality.questionPrompt:
### Checkpoint 1.1: Wire Protocol & Trust Boundaries
Toggle between **A2UI** and **MCP Apps** in the embedded simulator below, then answer the question:

{{WIDGET_EMBED}}

When a remote agent streams a UI across an untrusted enterprise boundary using **Google A2UI v0.9**, what is actually transmitted over the wire to construct the UI?
options:
Option A: Declarative JSONL packets (`createSurface`, `updateComponents`, `updateDataModel`) referencing pre-approved host catalog IDs and JSON Pointer paths:
```json
{"id": "canary-slider", "component": "Slider", "value": {"path": "/canaryPercent"}}
```

Option B: A self-contained HTML/JS string mounted inside a sandboxed `<iframe srcdoc="...">` via `_meta.ui.resourceUri`:
```json
{"_meta": {"ui": {"resourceUri": "ui://canary-studio/widget.html"}}}
```
Option C: Raw Tailwind CSS and inline `<script>` tags synthesized on the fly by the LLM and executed via `eval()` in the host DOM.

1.diagnosis: You selected the **MCP Apps (`SEP-1865`)** pattern! MCP Apps serve pre-built HTML/JS bundles via `ui://` resource URIs inside a sandboxed iframe. In contrast, **A2UI** never transmits HTML or JS—it streams declarative JSONL component IDs (`Card`, `Slider`, `Button`) mapped to the host app's native widget catalog.

2.diagnosis: A2UI specifically eliminates LLM-generated executable HTML/JS to prevent XSS and allow native rendering in non-web hosts like Flutter and SwiftUI.

remediationModality.questionPrompt:
### Remediation 1.1 (Alternative View: Wire Diff & Architecture Flow)
Let's look at the exact wire difference between **MCP Apps (`ui://` HTML iframe)** and **A2UI (Declarative Catalog JSONL)**:

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  subgraph A2UI["A2UI (Zero Executable Code)"]
    Ag1["Agent"] -->|"JSONL: {component: 'Slider', value: {path: '/pct'}}"| Cat["Native Host Catalog (Lit / Flutter)"]
  end
  subgraph MCP["MCP Apps (Sandboxed Iframe Code)"]
    Srv["MCP Server"] -->|"ui:// HTML + <script>"| Ifr["Sandboxed <iframe>"]
  end
```

```diff
--- MCP_App_Resource_Payload (Executable HTML/JS in Iframe)
+++ A2UI_v0.9_Wire_Payload (Declarative JSONL Component Graph)
- <input id="slider" type="range" oninput="window.parent.postMessage(...)" />
+ {"updateComponents": {"surfaceId": "main", "components": [
+   {"id": "slider", "component": "Slider", "value": {"path": "/weight"}}
+ ]}}
```

Suppose you are building a **native iOS/Flutter mobile client** that cannot safely execute arbitrary LLM-generated `<script>` tags, and you need to update a slider's value from `15` to `50` without re-sending the UI layout. Which A2UI message does the agent stream?
options:
Option A: A state-only `updateDataModel` JSONL packet targeting the bound JSON Pointer path:
```json
{"updateDataModel": {"surfaceId": "main", "path": "/weight", "value": 50}}
```
Option B: A `ui/notifications/tool-result` postMessage sent into a nested `<iframe sandbox="allow-scripts">`.
Option C: A full HTML page reload with `<input value="50">`.

nodes.title: 2. Bi-Directional Callbacks & Constrained Decoding Schemas
nodes.objective: Understand how UI callbacks return to the agent in A2UI (`userAction`), MCP Apps (`postMessage` JSON-RPC 2.0), and Gemini `response_schema`.

primaryModality.questionPrompt:
### Checkpoint 1.2: Why Untyped `dict[str, Any]` Fails in `updateDataModel`
When using the Google Antigravity SDK (`LocalAgentConfig(response_schema=...)`) to generate an A2UI `updateDataModel` payload, inspect what happens if `data_model` is typed as `dict[str, Any]` vs. a strongly typed Pydantic model:

```diff
--- a/example1_a2ui_rollout.py (Produces empty {"value": {}} in Gemini constrained decoding)
+++ b/example1_a2ui_rollout.py (Populates all bound JSON Pointer keys)
@@ -72,4 +72,9 @@
+class CanaryDataModel(pydantic.BaseModel):
+    service: str
+    canaryPercent: int
+    status: str
+
 class A2UITurnResponse(pydantic.BaseModel):
     surface_id: str
-    data_model: dict[str, Any] = pydantic.Field(default_factory=dict)
+    data_model: CanaryDataModel
```

Why did `data_model: dict[str, Any]` cause `gemini-3.8-flash` to emit `{"updateDataModel": {"value": {}}}`?
options: Option A: In Gemini constrained decoding (`response_schema`), an untyped `dict[str, Any]` compiles to an OpenAPI `OBJECT` with zero defined properties, forcing the decoder to emit `{}`.
Option B: A2UI v0.9 forbids sending `updateDataModel` on the first turn of a session.
Option C: Pydantic v2 automatically strips dictionary values when serializing to JSONL.

1.diagnosis: A2UI v0.9 encourages streaming `createSurface` + `updateComponents` + `updateDataModel` together on Turn 1 so all JSON Pointers (`{"path": "/canaryPercent"}`) immediately hydrate.

2.diagnosis: Pydantic serializes `dict[str, Any]` fine if keys exist; the bug happens upstream during **LLM constrained token decoding**, where Gemini's grammar compiler requires explicit schema properties.

remediationModality.questionPrompt:
### Remediation 1.2 (Execution Trace: Schema Grammar Compilation)
Trace how `response_schema` is compiled into token-level grammar constraints by the Gemini API:

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
  participant SDK as Antigravity SDK
  participant Dec as Gemini Constrained Decoder
  SDK->>Dec: 1. Compiles Pydantic model -> OpenAPI Schema
  Note over Dec: dict[str, Any] -> {type: OBJECT, properties: {}}
  Note over Dec: CanaryDataModel -> {type: OBJECT, properties: {service, canaryPercent, status}}
  Dec-->>SDK: 2. Only allows tokens matching declared properties!
```

If you need an A2UI `response_schema` where the agent can emit arbitrary dynamic keys into `updateDataModel` while still satisfying Gemini's strict property requirement, which Pydantic structure works?
options:
Option A: Use an explicit `list[DataModelEntry]` with typed `path` and value fields, then convert to a dict in Python:
```python
class DataModelEntry(pydantic.BaseModel):
    path: str
    int_val: int | None = None
    str_val: str | None = None
```
Option B: Keep `dict[object, object]` and set `temperature=2.0`.
Option C: Remove `surface_id` from the schema.
